text:
alex: heads-up — spotted a regression in mixed-precision paths when the continuous-batcher sees broad seq len distribution. FP8 path is ~12-18% slower than expected for a subset of requests. digging in now. :thinking:

kevin: reproable on staging? any uploads of profiler traces?

alex: repro on staging and a small slice of prod traffic (can share anon trace). profiler shows kernel selection flipping to FP8 kernels more often when batch shapes have a long tail (few long seqs, many short). interestingly CPU time for selector jumps. pasted sample from pprof: 
```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
12.3s  24.6% 24.6% 12.3s  24.6%  runtime.selectKernel
8.2s   16.4% 41.0% 8.2s   16.4%  runtime.fp8_ker_exec
6.1s   12.2% 53.2% 6.1s   12.2%  runtime.int8_ker_exec
3.9s    7.8% 61.0% 3.9s    7.8%  runtime.kv_cache_lookup
```

alex: selector is doing max_seq rounding and then picks kernel by block fit + quantization preference. with many short requests and a few long ones, rounding pushes the batch into shapes that favor FP8 kernels (because FP8 kernels are tuned for larger blocks), but padding waste for the many short ones kills throughput.

:tasha: that matches the histogram i dumped from continuous-batcher. shape distribution for the minute sample: [8: 52%, 16: 22%, 64: 3%, 128: 1%, variable: 22%]. median is 8 but max/selector sees 128.

alex: exact — current selector uses max(seq_lengths) per batch. suggestion: change cost function to weight by effective token waste = sum((chosen_block - seq) * batch_count) and pick kernel that minimizes (compute_cost_per_token * tokens + overhead). basically prefer a kernel with slightly suboptimal peak throughput if it reduces pad waste a lot.

kevin: can we compute that cheaply in the hot path? selector is on the CPU fast path and adding per-bucket sums might regress.

dmitri: we can maintain a compact histogram in the batch (buckets: 1-8,9-16,17-32,33-64,65-128,128+) and estimate waste quickly. one pass O(buckets) and a couple multiplies. cheap.

alex: proof-of-concept patch attached (small pseudo):
```
// bucket counts precomputed on enqueue
int buckets[6];
for each kernel k {
  int block = k.block_size;
  int waste = 0;
  for b in buckets:
    waste += max(0, block - bucket_max_len[b]) * buckets[b];
  score[k] = k.estimated_cycles * expected_tokens + waste * cost_of_padding;
}
choose min score
```

:tasha: nice. we should also account for KV cache hotness. if most short requests hit KV and don't re-run full transformer, pad cost is irrelevant. i saw kv_cache_lookup percentage at ~7.8% in the trace but that might be higher for conversational workloads.

alex: good call — i added a multiplier to reduce padding penalty for requests with kv_hit_rate > 0.7. if kv_hit_rate is high, prefer block sizes that reduce kernel launch overhead instead.

kevin: what about quant calibration effects? earlier experiments showed FP8 calibration tables sometimes push accum range that increases kernel compute (more dequant ops) — could be contributing?

alex: yes — we saw a small spike in fp8_ker_exec cycles after last calibration rollout. FP8 kernels are faster per-token normally, but if calibration causes additional per-token corrections (e.g., rescale+clamp) we're seeing higher cycles. i captured a microtrace showing extra instructions in the hot loop.

perf-bot: [alert] regression-delta: FP8 path median latency +14.2% over baseline (past 30m). linked traces: s3://redwood-perf/1777777777/fp8-trace.pb.

kevin: ok next steps:
- dmitri: land cheap histogram-based selector and benchmark on staging (owner)
- tasha: run A/B on 10% prod traffic with selector change + disable last FP8 calibration (rollback) (owner)
- alex: add unit test for kv_hit_rate path and a microbench for padding cost constant tuning (owner)

dmitri: i'll spin up a bench harness that replays the shape distribution and kv flags. estimate 1 day to have numbers.

tasha: i'll coordinate the A/B config and add metrics (pad_waste_tokens counter, kernel_choice distribution). will watch for tail latency regressions. ETA EOD tomorrow. :eyes: 

kevin: if selector patch is cheap and helps, we can roll it into the continuous-batcher fast path. otherwise fallback to a tuned threshold where if max_seq / median_seq > X, prefer median-based kernel.

alex: also FYI — noticed some requests pin to FP8 int fusion kernels that don't support certain sequence mod shapes (e.g., lengths not divisible by 16), causing fallback to slower generic path. we'll add kernel compatibility masks to selector to avoid oscillation.

dmitri: noted. will include kernel_compatibility bitmask in the score calculation.

kevin: good. timeline: patch + staging bench by tomorrow, A/B config next day, monitor 72h and decide rollback if we see >5% median regression.

alex: uploading anonymized trace and pprof to the ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [info] created perf-ticket #INF-4621 for this regression.
